title: Getting in and getting comfortable
notes: All 13 questions answered from a direct full-text read of the official 2008 Fit Owner's Manual PDF (S-001, techinfo.honda.com, via r.jina.ai per ADAPT-2) -- Tier 1, Confidence: high on every fact, 0 UNVERIFIED. Notable: base (non-Sport) trim confirmed to have NO remote keyless entry (entire Remote Transmitter section is Sport-only) but DOES have power mirrors (Canadian-DX-only exclusion does not apply to US base) and a tilt-only steering wheel (no telescoping found anywhere in the 282-page manual/index). 2 procedure cards written: Open the hood; Adjust your seat and mirrors before driving. No new conflicts logged; F-WP03-009 corroborates (does not conflict with) WP-01's C-009 tilt-wheel claim at higher confidence.

title: Driving
notes: 16 fact cards, all sourced to a direct curl read (not a search snippet) of the hfitinfo.com mirror of the Honda Fit 2001-2008 first-generation owner's manual (Tier 1) plus fueleconomy.gov EPA driving tips (Tier 2). Confirmed the base (non-Sport) automatic HAS a full P-R-N-D-D3-2-1 gate (text + labeled shift-gate diagram), contrary to the plan's caution that some Fit automatics might only have D and one lower gear; Sport model instead has P-R-N-D-S with paddle shifters. Confirmed manual shift pattern, 5th-to-reverse lockout mechanism, recommended shift-point speeds (15/27/39/53 mph), 600-mile/1,000 km break-in period with its specific dos/don'ts, owner's-manual and EPA fuel economy tips, snow-tire and tire-chain guidance (chains: front only, SAE Class S cable-type, no metal link chains), and trailer towing (manual states the car is not designed to tow a trailer at all and doing so can void the warranty -- no numeric rating given). 1 fact (F-WP06-009, hill start method) left UNVERIFIED as a Honda-documented feature/procedure -- confirmed absent from the manual's full Driving chapter table of contents; this generation predates Hill Start Assist. Procedure cards WP-06-1 (hill start) and WP-06-2 (first manual drive) use a general three-pedal technique grounded in this vehicle's own documented clutch/parking-brake behavior, explicitly flagged as general technique rather than a Honda-published Fit procedure. No conflicts found this pass (single coherent primary source); none logged to queue/conflicts.md.
